# Graphing named-lock and producer-claim acquisitions off one metric

`rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total` counts both named-lock acquisitions and
producer-claim acquisitions, distinguished by label, and reports contention as
its own series.

## Open the metrics listener

```bash
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -p 9465:9464 \
  -e RIMSKY_METRICS_HOST=0.0.0.0 -e RIMSKY_METRICS_PORT=9464 \
  -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" \
  rimsky-all-in-one:<tag>
```

## The deployment

A named lock of limit 1 beside a claim producer:

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers:
  files:
    endpoint: "producer:9100"
    protocols: ["claim_producer"]
    write_semantics_allowed: ["sync"]
named_locks:
  gate:
    limit: 1
executors:
  "third-party":
    transport: grpc
    endpoint: "peer:9400"
    protocols: ["executor"]
```

## The template

Three slow nodes contend for the lock while a fourth takes a producer claim.

```yaml
name: lockmetric
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: slow_a
    executor: third-party
    locks:
      - name: gate
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome:  {type: string, default: ok}
          sleep_ms: {type: integer, default: 1500}

  # slow_b and slow_c are identical

  - type: claimer
    executor: third-party
    claim_producers:
      - name: files
        selector: notes/a.txt
        intent: rw
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: retry}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          outcome:  {type: string, default: ok}
          sleep_ms: {type: integer, default: 0}
```

## Scrape it

```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9465/metrics | grep '^rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total'
```

## What the product reports

```
# HELP rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total ...
# TYPE rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total counter
rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total{acquirer="gate",acquirer_kind="named_lock",intent="acquired"} 3
rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total{acquirer="gate",acquirer_kind="named_lock",intent="unavailable"} 20
rimsky_claim_acquisitions_total{acquirer="files",acquirer_kind="producer",intent="acquired"} 1
```

One counter family carries both acquirer kinds as label values: the named lock
at three acquisitions — one per holder — beside the producer at one. An operator
graphs both off one metric rather than hunting in separate places.

The lock appears on its own labelled series, named by `acquirer`.

Contention is its own series, `intent="unavailable"`, distinct from the
acquisition count. That is the saturation signal to graph and alert on, read
directly from the metrics surface instead of reconstructed from the event log.
